## Framing the choice

::: {.kicker}
AWS vs local
:::

:::: {.grid-2}
::: {.card .green}
::: {.label}
Local strengths
:::

- Closest match to the current framework
- We do this already for IRIS
- We can optimize for the hardware we have
- Lower recurring cost if utilization stays steady
:::

::: {.card .blue}
::: {.label}
AWS strengths
:::

- Can scale up for reprocessing
- AWS runs the database and storage; off-site copies are easy
  - "Less" IT work
- Pay-for-use "can" make the bill predictable
- Possible path for larger-scale L3 or campaign reprocessing
:::
::::

::: {.banner}
PUNCH did not have any numbers (lost in an email migration) but said once they worked out egress, it was most of the bill
:::

:::: {.grid-2 .compact}
::: {.card .blue}
::: {.label}
Data and pricing
:::

- Oregon On-Demand prices checked 23 Sep 2026; tax and support excluded
- 389 GB ({{< var cost.l0_gib >}} GiB) of L0; L1 {{< var cost.l1_gib >}} GiB and L2 {{< var cost.l2_gib >}} GiB from local benchmark size ratios
- About {{< var cost.l0_files >}} L0 files (~2-3 MB each)
- Storage is the monthly price ÷ 30; compute runs the full 24 h
- L2 downloaded once, straight from S3, at $0.09/GB; the free 100 GB assumed used up (else $9 less)
- L1 omitted from S3
:::

::: {.card .amber}
::: {.label}
Per line item
:::

- EC2: one `m7i.2xlarge` at {{< var cost.ec2_rate >}}/h, Dagster on the same host, 8 vCPUs (4th Gen Xeon, Sapphire Rapids) and 32 GiB of memory
- RDS: `db.m7g.large` Single-AZ at {{< var cost.rds_rate >}}/h, plus 100 GiB of gp3
- Disk: proposed 1 TiB, including 132 GiB system/state. Requires verified upload, eviction and restore; current code keeps every file
- S3, requests, network and logs bar: one day of L0, L2 and L3 in S3 Standard ({{< var cost.day_s3 >}}), {{< var cost.day_puts >}} PUTs + {{< var cost.day_gets >}} GETs ({{< var cost.day_req >}}), NAT + one public IPv4 ({{< var cost.day_nat >}}), database and disk backups ({{< var cost.day_backups >}}), logs and secrets ({{< var cost.day_logs >}})
- Logs/CloudWatch and secrets are allowances. Extra requests, cross-AZ/Region traffic and further downloads are unmeasured
:::
::::

## Monthly cost at year 1 : L0 → L2 + storage

::: {.kicker}
AWS vs local
:::

|                                          |           Low |          High | What decides it                                          |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------: | ------------: | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Always on: EC2, RDS, NAT, requests, backups, logs | {{< var cost.m_always >}} | {{< var cost.m_always >}} | Instance sizes; agreed Single-AZ database |
| EC2 disk, proposed 1 TiB                  | {{< var cost.m_ebs >}} | {{< var cost.m_ebs >}} | Pipeline must delete local files after upload (not built) |
| S3 storage                               | {{< var cost.m_s3_lo >}} | {{< var cost.m_s3_hi >}} | Whether L2 and L3 are kept after 90 days |
| Egress (data leaving AWS)                | {{< var cost.m_eg_lo >}} | {{< var cost.m_eg_hi >}} | What is downloaded, and how often |
| **Total per month**                      | **{{< var cost.m_lo >}}** | **{{< var cost.m_hi >}}** | |

- **S3 storage grows with the mission:** one day of L0, L2 and L3 costs {{< var cost.day_s3 >}} to store.
  At year 1: L0 is 30 days in Standard plus 335 in Glacier; L2/L3 are 90 days in Standard, with older data optionally in Glacier Instant Retrieval. Metadata and transitions are included.
  Moving about {{< var cost.l0_files >}} L0 files a day into Glacier adds {{< var cost.m_l0_moves >}} a month
- **Egress depends on who downloads what:** the low end ({{< var cost.m_eg_lo >}}) is 30 daily L2 downloads, a little cheaper because the first 100 GB a month are free.
  The high case adds optional L0/NASA copies and user downloads at {{< var cost.share_hi >}} of new monthly L2/L3 bytes
- **Calendar convention:** 30 daily batches and 720 hours. AWS bills actual usage; 730 hours is an annual-average planning convention

## Storage over the mission

::: {.kicker}
AWS vs local
:::

:::: {.grid-2}
::: {.card .blue}
::: {.label}
S3: where data is kept
:::

- **L0, kept for the mission:** 30 days in S3 Standard, then Glacier Flexible Retrieval ({{< var cost.glacier_rate >}}/GB-month; bulk retrieval bytes/requests are free; temporary storage and egress are extra). Each year kept adds about {{< var cost.l0_growth >}} a month
- About {{< var cost.l0_files >}} L0 files a day cost {{< var cost.m_l0_moves >}} a month just to move into Glacier
- **L1 comparison:** discard and rebuild, or retain 90 days; the latter adds roughly {{< var cost.l1_90d >}}/month plus PUTs
- **L2 + L3:** 90 days is about {{< var cost.l23_90d >}} a month; keeping them for the mission in Glacier Instant Retrieval adds about {{< var cost.l23_growth >}} a month per year
:::

::: {.card .amber}
::: {.label}
EC2 disk: where the pipeline works
:::

- The pipeline only works on a normal disk (EBS, attached to the EC2 instance); it can't read or write S3 directly
- Proposed: stage L0, process, verify S3 exports, then evict and restore on demand. A generic S3 mount hasn't been tested
- One full day plus state needs **{{< var cost.ebs_min >}} GiB** before temporary space. A 1 TiB target only works if batch sizes are measured and capped
- If nothing is deleted, as today: EBS alone is **{{< var cost.ebs_30 >}}/month at day 30**, {{< var cost.ebs_365 >}} at year 1
:::
::::

::: {.banner}
After year 1, S3 costs {{< var cost.s3_y1 >}} a month and grows by {{< var cost.s3_growth >}} a month for each further year
:::

## L2 → L3 on two GPUs in the cloud

::: {.kicker}
AWS vs local
:::

| Two GPUs                          | Per hour | 8 h a day, per month | 24 h a day, per month |
| --------------------------------- | -------: | -------------------: | --------------------: |
| 2× T4 16 GB | {{< var cost.gpu_t4 >}} | {{< var cost.gpu_t4_8 >}} | {{< var cost.gpu_t4_24 >}} |
| 2× L4 24 GB | {{< var cost.gpu_l4 >}} | {{< var cost.gpu_l4_8 >}} | {{< var cost.gpu_l4_24 >}} |
| 2× A10G 24 GB | {{< var cost.gpu_a10g >}} | {{< var cost.gpu_a10g_8 >}} | {{< var cost.gpu_a10g_24 >}} |
| **2× A10G 24 GB, 16 vCPU / 64 GiB each (chosen for now)** | **{{< var cost.gpu_g54 >}}** | **{{< var cost.gpu_g54_8 >}}** | **{{< var cost.gpu_g54_24 >}}** |
| 2× L40S 48 GB | {{< var cost.gpu_l40s >}} | {{< var cost.gpu_l40s_8 >}} | {{< var cost.gpu_l40s_24 >}} |
| 2× H100 80 GB | {{< var cost.gpu_h100 >}} | {{< var cost.gpu_h100_8 >}} | {{< var cost.gpu_h100_24 >}} |

::: {.compact}
**Selected for comparison: 2× `g5.4xlarge`.** Each has an A10G (24 GB), 16 vCPUs, 64 GiB RAM and 600 GB local NVMe
:::

:::: {.grid-2 .compact}
::: {.card .green}
::: {.label}
What it saves
:::

- Avoids the L2 download: {{< var cost.avoided_egress >}}/month, at the last tier's rate in each case
- Two L4s break even at {{< var cost.l4_hours >}} hours/day each, including a 64 GiB boot-disk allowance
- The selected `g5.4xlarge` pair breaks even at {{< var cost.l3_gpu_hours >}} hours/day each
:::

::: {.card .amber}
::: {.label}
What it doesn't
:::

- User L3 downloads still leave AWS; {{< var cost.shares >}} of new monthly L3 is {{< var cost.sci_l3 >}}/month at $0.09/GB before allowance
- Keep the pipeline and GPUs in the same Region: between Regions is $0.02/GB, about {{< var cost.xr_l2 >}} a month for L2 alone
- Required runtime and memory are still unmeasured
:::
::::

::: {.banner}
One GPU is half the price above
:::

| 4 | {{< var cost.proc_one_4 >}} | {{< var cost.proc_host_one_4 >}} | {{< var cost.proc_pair_4 >}} | {{< var cost.proc_host_pair_4 >}} |
| 8 | {{< var cost.proc_one_8 >}} | {{< var cost.proc_host_one_8 >}} | {{< var cost.proc_pair_8 >}} | {{< var cost.proc_host_pair_8 >}} |
| 12 | {{< var cost.proc_one_12 >}} | {{< var cost.proc_host_one_12 >}} | {{< var cost.proc_pair_12 >}} | {{< var cost.proc_host_pair_12 >}} |
| 24 | {{< var cost.proc_one_24 >}} | {{< var cost.proc_host_one_24 >}} | {{< var cost.proc_pair_24 >}} | {{< var cost.proc_host_pair_24 >}} |
:::
::::

::: {.banner .green}
Excludes S3 storage, S3 requests, all egress and any GPU scratch beyond the boot disks. On-Demand prices; no Spot, reservations or archive-tier savings assumed

My working assumption is that by splitting the machines, we can price each machine to what is required instead of wasting money on unused resources.
:::

## Assumptions to confirm

::: {.kicker}
AWS vs local
:::

:::: {.grid-2}
::: {.card .blue}
::: {.label}
Science and operations
:::

- GPU hours per day, and GPU memory, for L2 → L3
- User downloads below 25% of new monthly L2/L3; measure bytes/repeats and cache location/hit rate
- Compare both L1 policies and both L3 locations; confirm L2/L3 lifetime and optional L0/NASA exports
- L3 product definition: 124 or 366 GiB/day are alternatives; link a reproducible size report
:::

::: {.card .amber}
::: {.label}
Engineering
:::

- AWS speed is unmeasured. Locally, 2 workers did 33.6 GB/h on the heavy placeholder, so one day takes about 12 hours on a fast desktop
:::
::::

::: {.banner}
Base rates checked against AWS catalogs on 23 September 2026. Oregon prices; N. California is {{< var cost.nc_pct >}} higher. No work on optimizing cost has happened
:::
